exam.title: Design and Technology Paper 1 (17/1) - October/November 2010
exam.subject: Design and Technology
exam.description: Botswana Examinations Council, Junior Certificate Examination. Answer all 40 questions. Four possible answers are given for each; choose the one you think is correct.

questions.question: The tool shown below is used to mark out and check
questions.explanation: The tool shown is an engineer's try square (a blade pivoted on a stock). It is used to mark out and check 90° angles, for example when squaring a line across a piece of material or checking that two surfaces are square to each other.

questions.question: A plastic that is heated and shaped many times
questions.explanation: A thermoplastic softens every time it is heated and hardens again as it cools, without any permanent chemical change taking place. This property, which allows it to be reshaped over and over again, is known as plastic memory.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct symbol of first angle projection?
questions.explanation: In the first angle projection symbol the circular (end) view is drawn on the left and the frustum of the cone is drawn on the right with its large diameter nearest to the circle, narrowing away from it. This matches option D.

questions.question: Which of the following adhesives is used in building boats?
questions.explanation: Cascamite is a synthetic resin (urea-formaldehyde) adhesive that sets completely waterproof and boil-proof (WBP), which is why it is the standard glue used for exterior work and boat building.

questions.question: Which of the following statements will be considered when designing a toy for a child?
options: The use of lubricant on moving parts
questions.explanation: Toys for children must be finished safely: a dull, non-toxic, non-reflective finish avoids lead-based or glare-producing glossy paints and reduces the risk of glass-like splinters if the finish chips. Heavy materials, overly rigid constructions and lubricants on moving parts are all safety hazards for young children.

questions.question: Which of the following is a mandatory workshop safety sign?
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs (must-do instructions) are shown as a blue circle with a white symbol. Option B, the blue circle showing ear defenders, is the mandatory sign. The triangle (A) is a warning sign, the red circle with a diagonal bar (C) is a prohibition sign, and D is an information/general sign.

questions.question: Which of the structures shown below is the most rigid?
questions.explanation: A triangle is the only polygon whose shape cannot be distorted without changing the length of its sides, so a triangulated frame (A) is inherently the most rigid structure. The rectangular and irregular quadrilateral frames (B, C, D) can rack/distort unless braced.

questions.question: The diagram below shows two aluminium pieces joined using a rivet. Which of the following statements has been considered when joining the pieces together?
questions.explanation: The thickness of the material being joined determines the length of rivet shank required and the size of hole to be drilled, so it is the main factor considered when selecting a rivet for a joint.

questions.question: The diagram below shows a container for a pencil sharpener. Which of the following details is important to write on the container?
questions.explanation: A pencil sharpener is a durable, non-perishable product, so an expiry date does not apply. Standard packaging information for this kind of product includes the quantity of product contained inside the package.

questions.question: A metal which rusts contains
questions.explanation: Rust is the common name for iron oxide, which forms when iron (or an iron alloy such as steel) reacts with oxygen and moisture. Zinc, copper and aluminium do not rust, though they can corrode or tarnish in other ways.

questions.question: Which of the following boards consist of strips of wood joined together and faced with veneer on both sides?
questions.explanation: Blockboard is made from solid strips of softwood glued edge to edge to form a core, which is then faced with a veneer on both sides. Chipboard is made from compressed wood chips, hardboard from compressed wood fibres, and plywood from thin veneer layers glued with the grain alternating.

questions.question: Which of the following rivets can be used to join the two pieces of aluminium shown below?
questions.explanation: The diagram shows a joint where only one side of the work is accessible (the back of the curled/closed section cannot be reached to hold a rivet set or dolly). A pop (blind) rivet is specifically designed to be set from one side only, making it the suitable choice here.

questions.question: Which of the following is the safe way of disposing pieces of wood?
questions.explanation: Offcuts and waste wood in a school workshop should be placed in the designated waste bins for safe, controlled disposal, rather than burned, buried or incinerated by learners, which carries fire and safety risks.

questions.question: The diagram below shows an egg holder made from a 2 mm aluminium sheet. Which of the following is the correct order of stages in producing the holder?
questions.explanation: The sheet should be marked out first, then cut to size, then filed to remove burrs and bring it accurately to size while it is still flat (much easier than filing after bending), then bent to shape, and finally given an overall finish.

questions.question: Which of the following abrasives is suitable for finishing the egg holder?
questions.explanation: Wet and dry paper, used with water, produces a smooth, fine, scratch-free finish on sheet aluminium without overheating or scoring the surface, making it the most suitable abrasive for this job. Glass paper is intended for wood.

questions.question: Which of the following mechanisms can move the head of a toy sideways?
questions.explanation: A rack and pinion mechanism converts rotary motion into linear (side-to-side) motion, which is exactly the movement needed to push a toy's head sideways.

questions.question: What is a chord?
options: Part of a circle covered by an arc and straight line
A straight line which touches two parts of the circumference
A straight line which touches any point on the circumferences
Part of a circle bound by two radii at right angles and an arc
questions.explanation: A chord is a straight line joining any two points on the circumference of a circle. Option A describes a segment and option D describes a quadrant.

questions.question: Why is aluminium used to make aircraft bodies?
questions.explanation: Aluminium has a high strength-to-weight ratio; being light in weight while still being strong is the main reason it is chosen for aircraft construction, where reducing overall weight is critical.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct order of steps in the process of finishing the edges of plastics?
options: Wet and dry, brasso, filing, buffing
Filing, wet and dry, brasso, buffing
Brasso, wet and dry, filing, buffing
Buffing, filing, wet and dry, brasso
questions.explanation: Edges of plastic are first filed to shape and remove saw marks, then progressively smoothed with wet and dry paper, then polished with Brasso (metal/plastic polish), and finally buffed to a high shine on a buffing machine.

questions.question: The figure below shows an exploded view of a tea pot stand. What is the name of the joint labelled L?
questions.explanation: The joint labelled L is where two leg strips cross one another, each notched out to half their thickness so they interlock flush. This crossing joint is a cross halving joint.

questions.question: Which of the following finishes is suitable for the top?
questions.explanation: The top of a tea pot stand must withstand heat and spills from a hot teapot. Polyurethane varnish forms a tough, heat- and water-resistant film, making it the most suitable finish of the options given.

questions.question: The figure below shows an exploded view of a tea pot stand. Which of the following fixings would be suitable for joining the top to the base?
questions.explanation: Since the screw holes are drilled through the top disc, a countersunk head screw (A) is needed so the head seats flush with, or below, the surface, leaving the top flat so a hot teapot can stand on it safely.

questions.question: The figure below shows an acrylic bar which has to be bent to shape. Which of the following is the method of deforming acrylic?
questions.explanation: The diagram shows a narrow strip of acrylic clamped in a vice and bent over the jaw in stages after being heated along a line — this localised heating-and-bending process is called strip bending (line bending). Vacuum and press forming use heated sheet pulled or pressed into a mould, not a strip bent over an edge.

questions.question: The diagram below shows a power tool. What is the name of the tool?
questions.explanation: The tool has an electric motor with a soft mop/wheel mounted on each end of its spindle, used for polishing — this is a buffing machine.

questions.question: Which of the following is a safety precaution to be observed when using the tool?
questions.explanation: A buffing machine throws off polishing compound and can snag loose material. Goggles must always be worn to protect the eyes from flying debris and compound; gloves are avoided near rotating mops because they can be caught and drawn in.

questions.question: The figure below shows an isometric sketch of a machine block. Which of the following represents the front elevation of the block?
questions.explanation: Projecting the sloped top face and the stepped cut-out of the block squarely onto the front plane gives a rectangle with a single diagonal line running the full height from the front face to the top of the step, and the stepped recess outlined with a visible (solid) step line, as shown in option B.

questions.question: Which of the following metals is used for making brazing rods?
questions.explanation: Brazing rods are usually made of brass, an alloy of copper and zinc, which has a melting point below that of the steel or copper parts typically being joined.

questions.question: Which of the pulley mechanisms shown below requires the least effort to lift a 50 kilogram load?
questions.explanation: A block and tackle gains mechanical advantage from the number of pulleys/rope strands supporting the load — the more pulleys used, the less effort (force) is needed to lift the same load. Option D has the most pulleys, so it requires the least effort.

questions.question: The tool shown is used for making holes in
questions.explanation: The tool shown is a revolving punch plier, the standard hand tool used to punch round holes in leather, for example for belts and straps.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct method of shooting the work piece?
questions.explanation: When shooting (planing) a piece of wood on a shooting board, a waste/backing piece of timber must be clamped against the edge where the plane iron will exit the cut, supporting the grain so it does not split or break away. Option C shows a full waste block positioned to back up the exit edge.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct method of storing manufactured boards?
questions.explanation: Large sheets of manufactured board should be stored flat, stacked horizontally and separated by spacers between each sheet, which lets air circulate evenly and prevents the boards from warping or bowing. Leaning sheets upright against a wall (B and C) encourages them to bow over time.

questions.question: The figure below shows a gear mechanism which controls the minute and hour hands of an analogue clock. Which gears control the minute hand?
questions.explanation: The minute hand is mounted directly on the topmost arbor, which carries gear (i) meshing with gear (v) immediately below the hands. The lower gears (ii), (iii), (iv) and (vi) form the reduction train that drives the slower-turning hour hand.

questions.question: Which of the following set of gears will move in an anti-clockwise direction as gear (i) moves in a clockwise direction?
questions.explanation: In a meshing gear train, each gear turns opposite to the gear it directly meshes with, while gears fixed on the same shaft turn together. Gear (v) meshes directly with (i), so it turns anti-clockwise; (iv) and (iii) are carried on the same shafts as gears turning anti-clockwise, so they also turn anti-clockwise, while (vi), meshing with (iv), turns clockwise (the same way as gear (i)).

questions.question: In which of the circuit diagrams below will the LED light?
questions.explanation: In circuit B the transistor is correctly drawn as an NPN type (emitter arrow pointing outward, away from the base) with the switch and resistor driving the base, and the LED is correctly oriented so conventional current flows from the positive supply through the LED and collector-emitter junction to the negative rail when the transistor switches on. In circuit C the transistor symbol is reversed (drawn as PNP), and in circuit D the LED is connected the wrong way round for the direction current flows through that branch, so in both cases the LED will not light.

questions.question: The diagram below shows a jewellery tray made from copper. Which of the following shows the development of the tray?
questions.explanation: The tray's front comes to a folded point where the two sloped side panels meet. The correct development (net) must include the triangular fold allowance at that point so the panels can be folded up and joined to form the pointed front, as shown in option A.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct method of joining the sides together?
questions.explanation: The tray is made from thin copper sheet. Soft soldering is the standard method for joining thin sheet metal work such as this, giving a neat, leak-proof seam without the heat distortion that brazing would cause on thin material.

questions.question: The diagram below shows a bracket. Which of the following shows the sectional front elevation indicated by the arrows YY?
questions.explanation: Cutting along YY through the length of the bracket shows the solid handle and tapered body as hatched material, with the bored hole at the larger end appearing as an unhatched gap bounded by the solid end wall, as shown in option A.

questions.question: What is the function of the screen printing equipment shown in the diagram below?
options: To push ink through the screen mesh.
To collect ink from the screen mesh.
To print image onto the material.
To spread ink onto the material.
questions.explanation: The tool shown is a squeegee. In screen printing it is drawn across the screen to push ink through the open areas of the mesh and onto the material beneath.

questions.question: Which of the following would guide a designer when analysing a theme?
questions.explanation: When analysing a design theme, a designer breaks it down by considering its different aspects (for example social, aesthetic, economic and technical aspects) to fully understand what the theme requires before generating ideas.

questions.question: The diagram below shows a catapult. What energy is gathered by the stone as the rubber band is stretched?
questions.explanation: As the rubber band is stretched, elastic potential energy is stored in the system. When released, this stored potential energy converts into kinetic energy, launching the stone.
